title: The Line Down the Middle
paragraphs: Maya had never shared a bedroom before. Now, in the new house, she had to share one with Zara, her new stepsister. Zara was ten, a year younger than Maya, and she was loud. She sang while she brushed her hair, left her socks in little heaps on the floor and covered every surface with pencil shavings, because she drew on anything she could find.

On the fourth night, Maya fetched a roll of blue tape from the kitchen drawer. Without a word, she stuck a long line down the middle of the carpet, from the door to the window. 'That's my half,' she said. 'Don't cross it.' Zara glared at her. Then she made a sign that said KEEP OUT in enormous purple letters and propped it against her pillow.

For a whole week, the line stayed where it was. The girls brushed their teeth in silence and walked to school on opposite sides of the road. Mum and Zara's dad exchanged worried looks over dinner, but whenever they asked what was wrong, both girls said, 'Nothing.'

Then, one stormy Saturday evening, the lights went out. The whole house was plunged into darkness, and rain hammered against the window like handfuls of gravel. Maya reached under her bed for her torch. As she switched it on, a small, shaky voice came from the other side of the line. 'I don't like storms,' Zara whispered.

Zara was sitting bolt upright, clutching her pillow, and her face looked pale in the torchlight. Maya hesitated. She looked at the blue line. Then she stepped over it and sat down on the end of Zara's bed. 'Neither do I,' she admitted. 'But they're better with a torch.'

They pulled the duvet over their heads like a tent. At first, neither of them knew what to say. Then Zara said quietly, 'I miss my old house. There was a tree outside my window, and I used to draw it every day.'

Maya swallowed. 'I miss my old room too,' she said. 'I thought that if we shared, everything would change.' When Zara admitted that she had thought Maya hated her, Maya shook her head. 'I don't,' she said, and she was surprised to find that it was true.

To pass the time, Maya made up a story about a dragon who was afraid of the dark, and Zara drew it on the back of an old envelope. When the lights flickered on again an hour later, Mum found them still under the duvet, surrounded by drawings and giggling so much that they could hardly breathe.

The next morning, Maya peeled the blue tape off the carpet and squashed it into a sticky ball. Then the girls pinned Zara's dragon drawing to the wall between their beds. Underneath it, in Maya's neatest handwriting, was the title of their very first book together: The Dragon Who Needed a Torch.

options: To show how the girls' feelings about each other have changed.
To explain how to decorate a bedroom.
To show that blue is Maya's favourite colour.
To show that the carpet needed to be cleaned.

questions.prompt:
Give **two** impressions of Zara.
Use evidence from the text to support your answer.
questions.model: Zara is creative, because she 'drew on anything she could find' and drew Maya's dragon story on the back of an old envelope. She is also frightened of storms, because she says 'I don't like storms' in 'a small, shaky voice' and sits 'clutching her pillow'.
points: each different impression that is backed up with evidence from the text (1 mark each), such as:
loud or lively: 'she was loud' and 'She sang while she brushed her hair'
messy: she 'left her socks in little heaps on the floor' and covered every surface with pencil shavings
artistic or creative: she 'drew on anything she could find' and drew the dragon story
scared of storms: 'I don't like storms,' she said in 'a small, shaky voice'

questions.prompt:
Maya's feelings about Zara change during the story.
Explain how they change, using evidence from the text.
questions.model: At the start, Maya is annoyed with Zara and does not want to share a room with her. She sticks tape down the carpet and says, 'That's my half,' and then, 'Don't cross it.' By the end, Maya likes Zara and they have become friends. She tells Zara that she does not hate her and 'was surprised to find that it was true', and the girls make their first book together.
points: Explains that at first Maya is annoyed with Zara or does not want to share a room with her.
Explains that by the end Maya likes Zara, or that they have become friends.
Backs up both feelings with evidence, e.g. 'Don't cross it.' and 'she was surprised to find that it was true'.

questions.prompt:
At the end of the story, the girls make 'their very first book together'.
What do you think the girls will do next?
Use evidence from the text to support your prediction.
questions.model: I think they will make more books together, with Maya writing the stories and Zara drawing the pictures. The words 'their very first book' suggest that there will be more, and they worked well together when Maya 'made up a story about a dragon' and Zara 'drew it'. Now that the tape has gone, I think they will keep getting on well and share their room happily.
points: a sensible prediction (1 mark), e.g. they will make more books together; Maya will write the stories and Zara will draw the pictures; they will stay friends and share the room happily.

evidence from the text that supports the prediction (1 mark), e.g. 'their very first book' suggests there will be more; they enjoyed making the dragon story together and were 'giggling so much that they could hardly breathe'; Maya peeled the blue tape off the carpet.
